Mateo —

Quick heads-up: we pushed the demo out internally while we loop in our security and procurement teams. A couple of people also have travel next week so the original slot won’t work.

Security wants an extra 45–60 minute review focused on data residency, encryption, and audit logging. Procurement also wants to join to discuss contract milestones and PO timing — they asked for a short pre-read. Can we reblock and either (a) expand the session to 90–120 minutes or (b) split into a product demo followed by a governance deep-dive later the same day?

Subject: Re: Demo — need to add security & procurement; travel conflicts

Tom — thanks for the heads-up and for flagging the scope shift. Totally reasonable. We can accommodate either option but want to minimize churn for your stakeholders. Two proposals: 

1) Two-step same-day run: 40–45 minute product walkthrough (core flow + integration points) followed by a 60–75 minute governance workshop (security, data, procurement topics). That keeps the technical audience focused and gives the governance group time for deeper Q&A.

2) Single extended session: 100–120 minutes with a scheduled 10–15 minute break in the middle. Effective if most attendees can commit to one block.

Proposed windows (PDT): Wed Apr 14 — 09:00–11:00 or 13:00–15:00; Thu Apr 15 — 10:00–12:00.

Requests from our side before the governance block:
- Procurement: please share a short list of commercial questions (PO timeline, invoicing cadence, indemnities) — we’ll have sales/legal on standby.
- Security: if you have specific controls or evidence to review (e.g., KMS, private deployment requirements), send the checklist so we can bring our security owner.

I’ve attached a draft agenda (redwood-demo-agenda-v2.docx) and a redacted SOC2 extracts pack we can present. Marissa and Soojin — can you confirm availability for the governance block and whether we should pull in our security engineering lead? Karthik — can you own procurement alignment if they surface contract questions?

If it helps we can also run a short 20-minute pre-demo call for procurement to line up PO expectations.

—Mateo
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-demo-agenda-v2.docx (agenda, timings)
